facts.text: Big River sits on the west bank of the Colorado River, just north of the Arizona side of the state line.
The community’s 10.8 square miles of land include a small water area that once marked the historic border between California and Arizona.

In the early 2000s, the Mendocino Land Trust partnered with 20 conservation groups, 12 state and federal agencies, 17 private foundations, and 1,400 donors to raise $25.7 million for the Big River watershed.
That money bought the land, stopping commercial logging and opening the area to restoration of old‑growth forest and fish habitat.
The Land Trust still works with partners to extend conservation and restoration across the entire Big River watershed.
Visitors can explore the area on trails listed in the MLT Trail Guide, and the community hosts monthly volunteer days such as the Hare Creek Beach hike on May 4, 2026.
